newsitem.title: DENMARK: B&O sees solidly better H1 1996/97 result.
newsitem.headline: B&O sees solidly better H1 1996/97 result.

text.p: Danish audio/video/ television manufacturer Bang & Olufsen Holding A/S upwardly adjusted on Tuesday its half-year 1996/97 expectations, forecasting 25 percent better pre-tax profits on 15 percent higher turnover.

"B&O Holding expects to emerge from the first six months of the accounting year 1996/97 with turnover of 1.550 billion crowns and a pre-tax and minorities profit in the region of 165 million crowns," the company said in a statement.
B&O, Denmark's leading audio manufacturer, is 25 percent owned by Netherlands-based Philips Electronics NV.
The group makes stylishly-designed hi-tech audio and video products for the luxury market.
B&O added that it expected at least 10 percent higher turnover for the full year 1996/97 despite expectations of lower growth in the second half due to falling mobile telephone sales in the period.
"During the first half of 1996/97, B&O has seen growth within all its markets for all its products," the firm said.
B&O's first half 1995/96 turnover was 1.335 billion crowns, with pre-tax and minorities profits of 132 million crowns.
The group's full year net result for 1995/96 was 183 million crowns, with pre-tax profit at 272 million crowns on 2.717 billion crown turnover.
Last August, when B&O announced its full year 1995/96 result, it said it expected overall growth in sales and profits in 1996/97 without giving any precise estimates.
B&O unveils its interim 1996/97 result on January 29, 1997.
